title: Free shuttles and other scheduled services within San Francisco missing from the operators' GTFS: which are modeled, their schedules and sources, and which are left out
built: server/beta3/pipeline/shuttles.ts writes data/beta3/raw/shuttle/shuttles.gtfs.zip from this file, the saved UCSF schedule pages, and the PresidiGo GTFS; transit.ts reads it and the Mission Bay TMA GTFS as the feeds 'shuttle' and 'tma'

missionBayTMA.routes: East (Civic Center/Powell BART, 4th & King Caltrain, Mission Bay, Chase Center), West (Civic Center/Powell BART, Caltrain, Mission Bay west), Transbay-Caltrain (Salesforce Transit Center, Embarcadero, Caltrain, Mission Bay), CCA/Adobe (Civic Center BART to 8th & Hooper)
missionBayTMA.eligibility: free and open to the public (GTFS routes.txt eligibility_restricted 0; missionbaytma.org)
missionBayTMA.headways: about every 15-30 minutes on weekdays, 6am-7:45pm, from the GTFS
missionBayTMA.source: GTFS published by the TMA through Trillium, Mobility Database source 51 (mdb-latest mirror), feed version 09-Dec-2025, valid 2025-12-09 to 2026-07-12; the model reads a Wednesday inside it (2026-04-08)

ucsf.eligibility: UCSF faculty, staff, students, trainees, patients, and visitors ride free; not open to the general public. Modeled as: anyone may board at a UCSF site (campus stops below), but at BART, Castro, Japan Center, UC Law, and Rincon Center stops only riders bound for a zone within 450 m of a UCSF site may board (BLine.restrict; build.ts).
ucsf.use: UCSF 2026 Commute Survey (9,000 respondents): 12.1% of UCSF commuters use the UCSF shuttle (10.2% in 2024), and the shuttle carries 55% of trips between UCSF sites. No boardings are published.
ucsf.schedules: each route's published weekday timetable (Monday-Friday; pages revised June 2025 to July 2026), saved as data/beta3/raw/shuttle/ucsf-<route>.html

presidiGo.eligibility: free and open to all, except that weekday trips before 9:30am and every other trip 4:30-6pm need a Presidio GO pass (Presidio residents and employees). Downtown stops are set-down only toward downtown and pick-up only toward the Presidio, so the route carries only trips to and from the Presidio; its peak riders are the pass holders it is restricted to.
presidiGo.source: The Trust's GTFS, https://presidiobus.com/gtfs (published by GMV Syncromatics; Transitland feed f-presidigo~ca~us), fetched 2026-10-07 by fetch-data.ts into data/beta3/raw/presidigo/presidigo-gtfs.zip: feed version 6/27/2026, weekday and weekend calendars from 2026-06-27 with no end. Stops, the route's shape, and every trip come from it. The pass rule is the Trust's: https://presidio.gov/visit/getting-to-and-around-the-park/presidio-go-shuttle/presidio-go-downtown-shuttle-schedule/
presidiGo.license: Neither the feed (feed_info names GMV Syncromatics as publisher; no license file) nor Transitland's listing states a license. It is the Trust's public feed for trip planners, used here for research with attribution.
presidiGo.pickUpOnlyNote: the feed marks the downtown set-downs (pickup_type 1) but not the pick-ups toward the Presidio; the Trust's rule makes those pick-up only, so the route carries no trips within downtown
presidiGo.passTrips: trips needing a pass are modeled as route 'PresidiGo DT pass': weekday loops leaving the Presidio Transit Center before 9:30am, and those leaving downtown (Drumm and California) within 5 minutes of 4:30, 5, 5:30, and 6pm, the trips the Trust names. Anyone may board them at the Presidio stops; downtown and at Van Ness only riders bound for a zone within 450 m of a Presidio stop (pass holders work or live there).
presidiGo.before: Before October 2026 the route was written from the Trust's web pages: 39 weekday loops from the Presidio Transit Center (every 15 minutes 6:00-9:15am and 3:30-6:30pm, every 30 minutes 9:30am-3:00pm), a 55-minute loop, no weekend service, stops geocoded with Nominatim (Lombard Gate by hand), one stop each for Van Ness/Union and Letterman Digital Arts Center, and 18 pass trips.

ridership.value: more than 300,000 rides in 2025 on all routes, all days (12% more than 2024); 635,000 in 2019; in 2014 the Downtown route averaged 991 riders a weekday and the Around the Park routes 444
ridership.source: Presidio Trust press releases via search (https://presidio.gov/about/press/presidio-trust-modernizes-presidio-go-shuttle-fleet); Wikipedia Presidio Go Shuttle; PresidiGo Capital Plan Final Report (https://rosap.ntl.bts.gov/view/dot/38691/dot_38691_DS1.pdf)
